::: {#thm-pairs-language}
#### The language of the a-and-b checker

The language (@def-automaton-language) of the DFA $A$ of @exm-pairs-dfa is

$$
L(A) = \set{w \in \set{\mathtt{a}, \mathtt{b}}^* : \text{every } \mathtt{a} \text{ in } w \text{ is immediately followed by a } \mathtt{b}}.
$$

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

Sort the strings over $\set{\mathtt{a}, \mathtt{b}}$ into three classes:

- class 0: no two $\mathtt{a}$s in a row, and not ending in $\mathtt{a}$;
- class 1: no two $\mathtt{a}$s in a row, and ending in $\mathtt{a}$;
- class 2: two $\mathtt{a}$s in a row somewhere.

Every string is in exactly one class.
A string has every $\mathtt{a}$ immediately followed by a $\mathtt{b}$ exactly when it is in class 0,
since an $\mathtt{a}$ that is not followed by a $\mathtt{b}$ is followed either by an $\mathtt{a}$ (class 2) or by nothing (class 1).
Let $P(w)$ be the statement

$$
\text{if } w \text{ is in class } k, \text{ then } \delta^*(q_0, w) = q_k.
$$

We prove $P(w)$ for every $w$ by structural induction (@def-structural-induction) on the recursive definition of strings (@def-string).

**Base case.**
The empty string $\lambda$ is in class 0,
and $\delta^*(q_0, \lambda) = q_0$ (@def-extended-transition), so $P(\lambda)$ holds.

**Inductive step.**
Suppose $P(w)$, and let $x \in \set{\mathtt{a}, \mathtt{b}}$.
By @def-extended-transition, $\delta^*(q_0, w x) = \delta\paren{\delta^*(q_0, w), x}$.
We split into cases on the class of $w$.

- **$w$ in class 0.**
  By $P(w)$, $\delta^*(q_0, w) = q_0$.
  Since $w$ does not end in $\mathtt{a}$, adding $x$ makes no two $\mathtt{a}$s in a row,
  so $w x$ has none, as $w$ has none.
  If $x = \mathtt{a}$, then $w x$ is in class 1, and $\delta(q_0, \mathtt{a}) = q_1$.
  If $x = \mathtt{b}$, then $w x$ is in class 0, and $\delta(q_0, \mathtt{b}) = q_0$.
- **$w$ in class 1.**
  By $P(w)$, $\delta^*(q_0, w) = q_1$.
  If $x = \mathtt{a}$, then $w x$ ends in two $\mathtt{a}$s, so it is in class 2, and $\delta(q_1, \mathtt{a}) = q_2$.
  If $x = \mathtt{b}$, then $w x$ still has no two $\mathtt{a}$s in a row and ends in $\mathtt{b}$,
  so it is in class 0, and $\delta(q_1, \mathtt{b}) = q_0$.
- **$w$ in class 2.**
  By $P(w)$, $\delta^*(q_0, w) = q_2$.
  Then $w x$ has two $\mathtt{a}$s in a row too, so it is in class 2, and $\delta(q_2, x) = q_2$.

In every case $\delta^*(q_0, w x) = q_k$ for the class $k$ of $w x$, so $P(w x)$ holds.
By structural induction, $P(w)$ holds for every string $w$.

Now let $w$ be any string, in class $k$.
By $P(w)$, $\delta^*(q_0, w) = q_k$, and $A$ accepts $w$ (@def-accept) exactly when $q_k \in F = \set{q_0}$, that is, when $k = 0$.
So $A$ accepts exactly the strings of class 0, which are the strings with every $\mathtt{a}$ immediately followed by a $\mathtt{b}$.

:::

:::
